agent: Codex main session with read-only MiniMax M3.1 Flash CCR research workers
purpose: Consolidate capability-aware fusion policy options, exact samurai-to-VOID mask transforms, quantization precedents, and RAM/VRAM offloading options for high-sensitivity segmentation and inpainting.

implemented.weights: static scalar or per-frame entropy confidence
implemented.quorum: unweighted min_expert_support vote gate at support_threshold
implemented.calibration: label-free Bernoulli Dawid-Skene EM over at least three aligned tensor experts; anchor is report-only
implemented.execution: every expert is read for every batch; there is no routing, abstention, role, critic, or escalation state

real_pilot_ablation.scope: two trampoline frames, three model families, VOID primary mask used only for post-hoc evaluation

structural_findings: An expert below support_threshold contributes no vote but still retains its full weight in the average; two p=0.9 votes plus one p=0 abstention currently fuse to 0.60 rather than a renormalized 0.90.
With three highly agreeing experts, support=2 is almost inert and support=3 behaves like unanimity.
Small capability differences in the pilot could not be expressed through scalar weights; capability must affect abstention, exclusion, quorum mass, routing, or a second critique phase.
The shipped command-expert example has one tensor expert and cannot enter tensor calibration.
Per-frame agreement alone was not a reliable expert router in the two-frame pilot.
recommended_policy: Represent one vote per lab lineage and reject duplicate variants from the same provider/training stack.
Add structured roles: dense_anchor, semantic, boundary, affected_region, and critic; roles must not remain free text only.
Add explicit abstention and renormalize over active expert mass, with an active-mass floor and fail-closed behavior.
Use capability-weighted quorum mass, not merely a weighted average; capability scores remain label-free panel estimates rather than ground truth.
Escalate only high-disagreement frames: re-query the dissenting experts with prior masks and a critique/adjudication request.
Run critique as a second phase. The critic modifies or confirms a candidate; it must not silently become another first-phase vote.
The immediate implementation priority is explicit abstention plus active-mass renormalization because it fixes an existing inconsistency without new model APIs.

external_precedents.name: CogVideo official TorchAO CLI example
external_precedents.finding: INT8 weight-only and FP8 dynamic activation casting cover T5, transformer, and VAE; FP8 is documented for H100-or-higher NVIDIA GPUs.

external_precedents.name: Diffusers TorchAO
external_precedents.finding: Clean quantization hooks enter through from_pretrained/Accelerate and support Linear layers; CPU quantization plus model CPU offload is an explicit deployment pattern.

external_precedents.name: SVDQuant
external_precedents.finding: W4A4 with a high-precision low-rank outlier branch and fused kernels; publisher-reported 3.5x memory reduction and 3.0x speedup versus 4-bit weight-only on FLUX.1.

external_precedents.name: QVGen
external_precedents.finding: video-DiT QAT at 3-4 bits, including CogVideoX; auxiliary error modules are decayed to avoid permanent inference overhead.

external_precedents.name: Q-VDiT
external_precedents.finding: token-aware error compensation and temporal-maintenance distillation for video DiT, reported at W3A6.

external_precedents.name: DeltaQuant
external_precedents.finding: FP8 core tokens plus quantized spatiotemporal deltas and SVDQuant-style weights; publisher-reported Wan 2.2 model-size and memory reductions.

external_precedents.name: unsloth/sam3.1
external_precedents.finding: BF16, INT8, INT8-ConvRot, and FP8 artifacts with publisher-reported mean mask IoU 0.9971-0.9984 versus BF16 on 53 prompts over 6 images.

external_precedents.name: Sparknight/sam3.1-int8-int4-convrot
external_precedents.finding: selective W8A8/W4A4 transformer linears with FP16 sensitive layers; 1.19 GiB and 0.98 GiB artifacts and publisher-reported 14.8%/27.8% RTX 3090 speedups.

void_blockers: custom transformer and VAE from_pretrained overrides bypass Diffusers quantization_config hooks
model_cpu_offload_and_qfloat8 loads FP8 and immediately casts back to BF16; it is not quantized compute
public NVFP4 remains a custom TorchAO integration rather than a TorchAoConfig switch
the convolution-heavy VAE is a poor fit for low-bit GEMM recipes and has non-16-divisible input/output channels
recommended_order: first qualify T5 FP8 or INT8 because it uses the stock transformers loader and is primarily a weight-residency win
second validate a hosted or prequantized SAM 3.1 artifact on real clips rather than trusting publisher spot metrics
third prototype VOID DiT W4A4 only with timestep-aware activation calibration and a fused or low-rank outlier path
leave the VAE BF16 until end-to-end profiling proves that it is a bottleneck

source_findings: unknown gpu_memory_mode silently selects full GPU load
model_cpu_offload and sequential_cpu_offload retain all weights in host RAM and move components or layers on demand
the qfloat8 mode is effectively BF16 after load and its conversion wrapper is a BF16-to-BF16 round trip
Pass 2 hardcodes model CPU offload and has no FP8 or sequential alternative
Pass 2 moves transformer, VAE, and T5 fully to GPU before enabling offload, creating an avoidable startup spike
Pass 2 custom loading defaults to low_cpu_mem_usage=False and can hold a model plus checkpoint state dict transiently
vae.enable_tiling and enable_slicing are never called by VOID; its existing encode/decode helpers do batch in groups of 8 and split convolution inputs above 2 GiB
Pass 1 hardcodes 30 inference steps and ignores config.video_model.num_inference_steps
temporal_multidiffusion_stride has a pipeline parameter but predict_v2v never passes it; config misspells it temproal_multidiffusion_stride
samurai's Pass 1 command does not forward config.seed, so pinned VOID uses its config.system.seed
the Pass 2 batch shell passes unsupported --gwf_dir and fails at argparse
warped-noise generation imports the external rp/CommonSource Go-with-the-Flow path and may install dependencies at runtime; the in-repo RAFT module is not used
